topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digit Emergence
target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of Newtonian mechanics

outline.topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digit Emergence
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of Newtonian mechanics

sections.title: The Hook: An Unexpected Discovery
sections.content: Introduce the counter-intuitive puzzle: How can a series of simple block collisions compute the digits of Pi? Present a visual of two blocks sliding on a frictionless surface towards a wall.
sections.example: A small block (mass m) and a large block (mass M=100m) sliding on a frictionless floor.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly review Conservation of Momentum and Conservation of Kinetic Energy. Explain that elastic collisions between blocks follow these two laws, leading to a system of equations that define the velocity updates.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'phase space' plot where the velocity of block A is the x-axis and block B is the y-axis, forming a circular arc path.

sections.title: Geometric Mapping: The Circle Connection
sections.content: Explain that the velocity states of the two blocks can be mapped onto a circle. As collisions occur, the velocity vector rotates by a specific angle. The total number of collisions corresponds to the arc length covered, mapping to Pi.
sections.example: An animation showing the velocity vector rotating around a circle every time a collision occurs; the total rotation angle is proportional to the square root of the mass ratio.

sections.title: Scaling Powers of 100
sections.content: Demonstrate that as the mass ratio M/m increases by factors of 100 (100, 10,000, 1,000,000), the number of collisions matches the digits of Pi (3, 31, 314, etc.).
sections.example: A digital counter display next to the colliding blocks showing the digits '3.14...' ticking up as the mass of the larger block increases.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Synthesize why this works: The problem is a discrete manifestation of a continuous rotation in phase space. Conclude that Pi appears whenever we look at the 'geometry' of conservation laws.
sections.example: A final visual summary: 1. Set up blocks, 2. Count collisions, 3. Reveal Pi.

storyboard.title: The Hook: An Unexpected Discovery
lecture_lines: Consider two blocks sliding toward a wall.
Small block m hits large block M.
Collisions produce digits of Pi. Amazing!
animations: Fade in a large, glowing blue Circle labeled 'C' at center. Color: #4169E1.
Flash the Circle 'C' three times to draw focus.
Transform Circle 'C' into a Square labeled 'S'. Color: #FF4500.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Collisions conserve both momentum and energy.
Velocity updates define a system of equations.
Phase space plots show circular paths.
animations: Fade in Vector 'V1' and Vector 'V2' in orange (#FFA500).
Move 'V1' and 'V2' to be tail-to-tip. Color: #FFA500.
Fade in Resultant Vector 'R' in green (#32CD32) showing conservation.

storyboard.title: Geometric Mapping: The Circle Connection
lecture_lines: Map velocity states onto a circle.
Each collision rotates the velocity vector.
Collision count relates to arc length.
Geometric mapping explains this Pi connection.
animations: Fade in a coordinate plane and a unit circle. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate a point moving along the arc of the circle. Color: #FFFF00.
Show the projection lines mapping to the x-axis. Color: #A9A9A9.

storyboard.title: Scaling Powers of 100
lecture_lines: Increase mass ratio by powers of 100.
Observe collision counts matching Pi digits.
animations: Display MathTex '100^n' in light blue (#ADD8E6) at center.
Scale the '100' element to 1.2x while 'n' stays static.
Display '10000' as the result of the transformation. Color: #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Conclusion and Intuition
lecture_lines: Phase space rotations yield discrete counts.
Geometry and physics are deeply linked.
animations: Fade in a summary node labeled 'Main Concept'. Color: #FFFFFF.
Connect the summary node to three branching sub-points. Color: #00FFFF.
Flash all elements once to signal completion.
